newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds end flat, quiet after issuance.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds end flat, quiet after issuance.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were static on Friday and did little more than track Treasuries to cap off a week of about $2.0 billion high-grade issuance, dealers said.
Market tone was characterized as firm, however, as evidenced by strong aftermarket trades of the new paper, traders said.

"The market was painfully quiet today but that doesn't say anything about the future," one trader said. "Fundamentals are still strong, deals get done and we should see more of the same with yields where they are."

Looking at the high-yielders, traders reported some dichotomy between new issues and secondary markets. New issues continued to trade up on the break, but dealers spied some secondary markets widening more than 20 basis points in spots.
Telecommunication paper was said to account for much of the fade, led by poorly traded TCI Communications Inc debt, some said. Late on Friday, Standard & Poor's said it may cut TCI's debt ratings.
Still, traders said Marvel Holdings took center stage with its zero couponed debt due 1998 trading down to 38 on Friday, almost half of their value just nine days ago.
The bonds traded at 43 on Thursday.

The debt began its slide after the Marvel Entertainment Group warned of a third quarter net loss that would put the company in violation of certain bank loan financial covenants. Moody's and Standard & Poor's have cut Marvel's debt ratings.

High-yielders up on Friday included Kaiser Aluminum and Chemical Corp's $175 million 144A senior notes at 99-5/8, up from Thursday's issued level of 99-1/2; Rayovac Corp's $100 million 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes at 101, up from par; and Aames Financial Corp's $150 million senior notes at 100-7/8, up from the issue price of 99.714.

High-yield issuance was termed moderate this week, but the street was poised for heavier volume through November, traders and analysts said. The anticipation over the calendar sapped aftermarket tone, traders said.

Separately, Trump-related debt was off one point or more in the wake of a lawsuit that alleges Donald Trump inflated the value of his Trump's Castle Casino Resort before its sale in September, one head trader said.
Trump Castles traded at 101 compared with 103 before the news, traders confirmed. Trump Atlantic City Funding $1.2 billion 11-1/4s of 2006 were down about one point.
In the governments market, prices ended a lackluster session little changed and the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 1/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
